subject: Finex: throughput/SLO follow-up (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 16:24:00 -0800
Subject: Finex call recap — throughput & SLO qualification

Hi Alex — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of what you outlined:
- Primary use: multi-tenant customer support assistant (chat + summarization) for Finex retail customers.
- Traffic profile: steady-state traffic during market hours with short 5-10 minute bursts around settlement windows.
- Target latency SLOs: p50 ~ <50ms token latency (streaming), p95 <150ms, p99 <300ms.
- Typical response size: mean ~220 tokens, tails up to 1,200 tokens for long summaries.

Questions we flagged for sizing (we'll handle these on our sizing call):
1) Confirm average concurrent active chats during peak 5-min bursts vs steady-state.
2) Clarify percentage of requests that use long-form summarization (>=500 tokens).
3) Any hard constraints on adding batching or caching in inference path.

Preliminary next steps:
- Rafael will run a throughput model based on the numbers you gave and send a sizing worksheet (attached).
- If possible, please share a small sample of anonymized request traces (timestamps + tokens/request) — helps us validate burst shape.
- Schedule a 30-minute sizing call next week with your infra lead + our SEs.

Attached: redwood-throughput-model.pdf (sizing worksheet template).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Neha — thanks for the recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency: steady-state ~80 active chats during market hours; peak bursts hit ~420 active chats for 4-8 minutes around settlement.
- Long-form summarization is ~12% of requests (these are background jobs but still need streaming).
- We can allow batching up to 100ms delay if that helps throughput, but prefer lower per-token latencies for streaming UX.

We'll put together a 48-hour sample of request timestamps and token counts and share via the Drive link you suggested.

Can Rafael and Marissa join a 30-minute call on Wed 24th at 11am ET?

— Alex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@finex.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finex call recap — throughput & SLO qualification (sizing details)

Thanks Alex — that data is exactly what we need. Based on the numbers so far I ran a quick back-of-envelope and a short checklist below. Please treat these as preliminary until we see the request traces.

Prelim sizing assumptions (from your notes):
- Steady-state concurrency: 80 active chats -> assume ~1.2 requests/sec per active chat average (typing + partial updates) -> ~96 RPS steady.
- Peak concurrency: 420 active chats -> ~1.4 RPS -> ~588 RPS peak.
- Average response length: 220 tokens (12% long-form 800 tokens average).

Estimated tokens/sec (client-side request tokens + generated tokens):
- Steady: average tokens per response = 220 -> tokens/sec = 220 * 96 ≈ 21,120 t/s.
- Peak: incorporate 12% long form -> effective avg tokens ≈ 220*0.88 + 800*0.12 = 273.6 -> tokens/sec = 273.6 * 588 ≈ 160,837 t/s.

QPS (requests/sec) numbers: steady ~96 QPS, peak ~588 QPS.

Concurrency planning notes (serving side):
- To hit streaming p50 ~ <50ms token latency and p95 <150ms, we'll prioritize CPU/GPU with low per-token overhead and prefer model variants with fast attention kernels.
- For peak bursts, we recommend dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) with autoscaling buffer and a short warm-up policy. Fallback policy: route to a slightly smaller model (quantized) if capacity saturates — we'll simulate impact on quality.

Operational notes / ask from Finex:
1) Share the 48h trace (timestamps + tokens/request + client-region) — that's the most actionable input for accurate capacity curves.
2) Indicate SLA priority for long-form summarization requests (are those allowed to be queued or must stream?).

I attached a quick worksheet with the above calculations and a couple of sizing scenarios (steady-only vs steady+peak burst). I'll bring the detailed perf model to the Wed 24 11am ET call.

Next steps I propose:
- You upload the trace to the Drive link by EOD Tue 23rd (or share a secure link).
- Wed 24th 11am ET call to validate numbers and agree on reserved capacity vs burst policy.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@finex.com>

Rafael / Neha — thanks for the breakdown, this is super helpful. We'll upload the 48h trace to the Drive link tonight.

Regarding long-form summarization: they must stream (customers want progressive output), but it's ok if we accept a slightly higher tail latency (p99 up to ~500ms) for those requests.

Wed 24th 11am ET works for the call — invite sent to Rafael, Neha, and Marissa. Looking forward to the sizing walkthrough.

— Alex
